package_info.package_manager: CDN (not a package manager, but a third-party JavaScript CDN service)
package_info.package_versions: All versions served after February 2024 (post-acquisition by Funnull)
package_info.why_malicious: After its acquisition by Funnull in February 2024, the polyfill.io CDN began serving malicious, obfuscated JavaScript payloads. These payloads dynamically inject additional scripts into websites, enabling user redirection, evasion of detection, and facilitating broader attacks such as formjacking and data exfiltration. The CDN is now an active supply chain attack vector and is no longer trustworthy for serving JavaScript.

execution_context.trigger: At runtime, when a user visits a website that loads the polyfill.io script.
execution_context.file_location: Dynamically served from cdn.polyfill.io and injected into the HTML <script> tag.
required_permissions: potential access to user input fields (if further payloads are loaded)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code checks if the user is not an admin and if analytics scripts are not present, then after a delay, dynamically creates and injects a <script> element with its src set to a typo-squatted analytics domain, resulting in the browser loading and executing additional malicious code, which can redirect the user or load further payloads.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code injects a script from a domain that closely mimics a legitimate analytics provider (e.g., 'googie-anaiytics.com'), a classic phishing and redirection tactic. The use of obfuscation, conditional execution, and delayed payload delivery are all hallmarks of evasive malware designed to avoid detection by security tools and researchers.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A polyfill service is expected to serve static, standards-compliant JavaScript for browser compatibility. It should never inject third-party scripts, perform user targeting, or redirect users to unrelated domains.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate analytics or A/B testing scripts may dynamically inject scripts, but only from trusted, well-known domains and with transparent user consent. They do not use typo-squatted domains or obfuscation.
key_indicators: Obfuscated JavaScript payloads served from a previously trusted CDN
Dynamic creation and injection of <script> elements with src pointing to typo-squatted analytics domains
Conditional execution based on user/admin status and presence of analytics scripts
Delayed execution to evade automated detection
Redirection to unrelated or malicious domains

execution_context.trigger: At runtime, when a user visits a website that loads the polyfill.io script.
execution_context.file_location: Dynamically served from cdn.polyfill.io and injected into the HTML <script> tag.
required_permissions: network access (to send or receive data)
DOM access (to inspect or modify the page)
user agent/environment detection (to determine device type and context)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code inspects the user's device type, admin status, and presence of analytics scripts; if the user is on a mobile device, not an admin, and analytics scripts are absent, it generates a payload based on HTTP headers and user environment, enabling targeted redirection or data exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Selective activation based on device type and environment is a common evasion technique, allowing the malware to avoid detection by security researchers and automated scanners. The code's ability to generate payloads dynamically based on HTTP headers and user context increases its effectiveness and stealth.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Polyfill scripts should not perform environment reconnaissance or selectively execute based on user/device context. Their only legitimate use is to provide browser compatibility features, not to target users or evade detection.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Feature detection for browser compatibility is legitimate, but using environment checks to evade detection or target specific users is not. Legitimate scripts do not use device or admin status to control malicious payload delivery.
key_indicators: Environment-based conditional logic to determine payload activation
Targeting of mobile devices while avoiding admin or analytics environments
Dynamic payload generation based on HTTP headers and user context
Reconnaissance of user environment for evasion and targeting

attack_chain.action: A website includes <script src="https://cdn.polyfill.io/...">, causing the user's browser to load and execute JavaScript from the CDN.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code from polyfill.io executes in the user's browser.

attack_chain.action: The malicious JavaScript inspects the user's environment, including user agent, HTTP headers, and the presence of analytics scripts or admin status.
attack_chain.leads_to: Conditional activation of the malicious payload based on device type and environment.

attack_chain.action: If the conditions are met (e.g., mobile device, not admin, no analytics), the code delays execution and injects a <script> tag pointing to a fake analytics domain.
attack_chain.leads_to: The browser loads and executes additional malicious code, potentially redirecting the user or loading further payloads.

attack_chain.action: The user is redirected to sports betting, pornographic, or other malicious sites, or is exposed to further attacks such as formjacking or data theft.
attack_chain.leads_to: Final goal: user compromise, data theft, or monetization via redirects.

behavioral_signatures: Dynamic injection of <script> elements with src attributes pointing to typo-squatted analytics domains (e.g., googie-anaiytics.com)
Obfuscated JavaScript payloads served from cdn.polyfill.io
Conditional execution logic based on user agent, admin status, or presence of analytics scripts
Delayed execution of injected scripts to evade detection
file_indicators: Injected <script> tags with src attributes referencing typo-squatted analytics domains (e.g., googie-anaiytics.com/gtags.js)
network_indicators: Redirects to sports betting, pornographic, or other suspicious domains initiated from browser sessions loading polyfill.io
Dynamic JavaScript payloads served from cdn.polyfill.io
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Scan website source code and network traffic for references to cdn.polyfill.io and typo-squatted analytics domains. Monitor for unexpected script injections and outbound requests to suspicious domains. Use browser instrumentation or web application firewalls to detect delayed script execution and conditional payload delivery. Flag obfuscated JavaScript served from third-party CDNs, especially if it performs environment checks or dynamic script injection.
